recent_posts.title: Trilio Extends Disaster Recovery Reach to Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
recent_posts.summary: Trilio has released a technology preview of Trilio Site Recovery (TSR), extending its storage-agnostic disaster recovery platform to Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization. TSR uses continuous replication to automate failover and failback across sites, now covering legacy monolithic applications running on KVMs encapsulated in containers via KubeVirt on Kubernetes clusters. The platform supports policy-based DR tied to SLAs and allows teams to validate recovery plans in isolated environments without affecting production. This addresses a key gap as organizations consolidate workloads onto Kubernetes to reduce infrastructure costs, particularly following Broadcom's acquisition of VMware which has driven interest in OpenShift Virtualization as an alternative.

recent_posts.title: How Kthena Router Supports Gateway API and Inference Extension
recent_posts.summary: Kthena Router now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API and Gateway API Inference Extension for routing AI/ML inference workloads. The post explains why these APIs matter — resolving global modelName conflicts in multitenant environments, enabling industry-standard interoperability, and supporting standardized inference routing via InferencePool and InferenceObjective resources. Step-by-step configuration examples cover enabling Gateway API via Helm, creating Gateways on different ports to isolate ModelRoutes with the same modelName, and deploying InferencePool resources with HTTPRoute for the Inference Extension. The post also contrasts these standard APIs with Kthena's native ModelRoute/ModelServer CRDs, which offer advanced features like prefill-decode disaggregation and weighted routing for production workloads.

recent_posts.title: EDB Highlights CloudNativePG 1.29, Previews Kubernetes-Native Data Protection at KubeCon Europe
recent_posts.summary: EnterpriseDB (EDB) announced CloudNativePG 1.29 at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026, an open source PostgreSQL operator for Kubernetes. The release adds modular extensions and supply chain security features, including software bill of materials support and AI-driven vector search options, reducing the need for custom database images. EDB also previewed an enterprise data protection solution for its commercial operator featuring zero data loss via native write-ahead log streaming, centralized management, disaster recovery, and end-to-end encryption. The announcements are framed around data sovereignty and EU Cyber Resilience Act compliance.

recent_posts.title: emma Technologies Launches Brownfield Onboarding for Unified Cloud and Kubernetes Governance
recent_posts.summary: emma Technologies announced Brownfield Onboarding at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026, enabling enterprises to bring existing VMware environments, Kubernetes clusters, and cloud accounts (AWS, Azure, GCP) under unified governance without migrating or disrupting workloads. The platform inventories infrastructure across the entire estate and uses an audit-first, non-destructive workflow for selectively importing resources into governed projects. It spans hyperscalers, regional providers, and AI-optimized clouds, covering deployment, cost management, and compliance under a single model.

recent_posts.title: Solo.io Launches agentevals Open Source Project, Contributes agentregistry to CNCF
recent_posts.summary: Solo.io announced two open source initiatives at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Europe 2026. The first is agentevals, a project for evaluating and benchmarking agentic AI behavior using OpenTelemetry to capture distributed agent interactions and score them against golden evaluation sets. It supports offline and online modes, trajectory matching, LLM-as-judge scoring, and works with any model emitting OpenTelemetry spans. The second is agentregistry, originally launched in November 2025, which Solo.io is contributing to the CNCF. It provides a centralized registry for cataloguing, discovering, and governing AI agents, MCP tools, and agent skills, with integrations for Kubernetes, AWS AgentCore, and Google Vertex AI.

recent_posts.title: How to get Kubernetes network observability using eBPF and Microsoft Retina
recent_posts.summary: Kubernetes networking is notoriously opaque, making incident diagnosis painful. eBPF offers kernel-level packet inspection with near-zero overhead, enabling true network observability rather than just monitoring. Microsoft Retina, an open-source CNI-agnostic DaemonSet-based tool, leverages eBPF to expose real-time network telemetry in Prometheus format. It operates in two modes: a metrics-only Legacy Mode for trend analysis and alerting, and a Hubble Mode for live traffic tracing that reveals exact packet drop reasons (NetworkPolicy denial, connection tracking timeouts, etc.) via the skb_drop_reason field. Retina requires no sidecars, no app code changes, and works across EKS, AKS, and GKE.

recent_posts.title: CNCF Chief: AI Inference Will Drive Increased Cloud Native Software Consumption
recent_posts.summary: CNCF executive director Jonathan Bryce predicts AI inference will massively increase cloud-native software consumption as more AI models deploy on Kubernetes clusters. Organizations will create smaller, specialized AI models running on inference engines, with AI agents invoking backend services instead of traditional graphical interfaces. This shift requires new orchestration tools beyond current CI/CD platforms, while software engineers' roles evolve toward platform engineering. The CNCF oversees 240+ projects, but maintainers face challenges from an influx of AI-generated code contributions of varying quality.

recent_posts.title: Chainguard Dashboard Provides Visibility into Pipeline for Creating Secure Container Images
recent_posts.summary: Chainguard launched a Fulfillment Dashboard that shows which secure container image projects are being prioritized based on customer requests. The dashboard aims to improve planning by providing timelines and reducing duplicate requests. With over 2,000 secure container images available and 400+ customers, Chainguard addresses growing concerns about software supply chain vulnerabilities. Many organizations have a false sense of security with containers, as the encapsulated software often contains vulnerabilities from outdated components. Proactively using secure container images can prevent vulnerabilities before they reach production and slow down deployment cycles.

recent_posts.title: Together AI Adds Container Interface to Managed Service for AI Models
recent_posts.summary: Together AI launched a Dedicated Container Interface for its managed cloud service, allowing teams to deploy AI inference models by packaging runtime, dependencies, and code into containers. The platform handles GPU provisioning, networking, health checks, and monitoring, with built-in support for distributed inference via PyTorch's torchrun. The service targets organizations deploying custom AI applications without managing on-premises GPU infrastructure, as two-thirds of organizations now run AI inference workloads on Kubernetes clusters.

recent_posts.title: Building an Enterprise-Ready AKS Cluster: Architecture, Networking and Security Baselines
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive blueprint for deploying production-grade Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters in regulated enterprise environments. Covers essential architecture patterns including system and user node pools, Azure CNI with Cilium networking for eBPF-powered performance, hub-and-spoke network topology with private endpoints, and security baselines like workload identity, private cluster mode, and image signing. Includes observability setup with Managed Prometheus and Grafana, disaster recovery patterns with multi-region failover, cost optimization strategies using spot instances, and governance controls through Azure Policy. Emphasizes GitOps-based deployment automation and zero-trust networking principles for banking, fintech, and government workloads.
